items.title: Building Micro-SaaS: Lessons from 0 to First €1000 with Claude
items.pt:
3 min read · 588 words


Hitting your first €1,000 in a micro-SaaS changes everything. It proves that strangers are willing to exchange hard-earned money for something you built. But getting there requires brutal prioritization: zero fluff, minimum infrastructure, and maximum leverage.

As solo developers, we can't compete on enterprise sales teams or massive ad budgets. We compete on speed and AI leverage. Here is how I built a niche document-processing micro-SaaS to €1K MRR using modern toolin

items.title: "Just one more prompt" kept stealing my evenings. So I set a 6 pm cutoff for 30 days.
items.pt:
AI tools made it easier than ever to turn an idea into something real. But I noticed an unexpected side effect: the faster I could build, the harder it became to stop.

One evening a small idea would turn into another prompt, another feature, and another hour of work. I was not working because of deadlines or pressure from anyone. I simply enjoyed building things and wanted to see what AI could do next. I wrote about the night it went too far here: a feature built at 3 AM, while feeding my baby.

items.title: FDE job postings in India grew 19x in a year. Here is the AI half backend engineers are missing.
items.pt:
In June 2026, India had nearly 19 times as many Forward Deployed Engineer job postings as a year earlier, on Indeed's count (Analytics India Magazine, reporting Indeed data, October 2026). In August they were still more than six times the year-earlier level.

The supply side moved far less. CIEL HR counted 52 organisations in India recruiting for the role in July 2026, and estimated that about 1,200 professionals in the country are fully equipped for it (CXOToday, reporting CIEL HR, August 2026)

items.pt: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models.
